Refactor duplicated policy calculations preserving behavior and keeping policies easy to change separately. UploadLimit(pro)=100, default=10; RetryLimit(pro)=10, default=3; GraceDays(pro)=10, default=3. Independently configured policies; equal current numbers are coincidental. # Baseline simulated decisions

Simulation only. I read the current go-code-refactor skill, go-style-core, the relevant PLAYBOOK sections, and the verification script's command interface. No Go commands or repository edits were performed.

## A: Simplify Load's nested branches

The edit scope is `Load` in `internal/cache/cache.go`. I would flatten exit branches into guard clauses and remove redundant `else` blocks, preserving predicate evaluation order, short-circuiting, returned values and errors, and side-effect/defer order. I would inspect neighboring code and tests to understand those constraints. I would avoid inventing an exact replacement body because the scenario supplies no `Load` source.

I would preview modernization for the cache package, review its suggestions, and manually apply only any transformation inside `Load` that supports the requested simplification. The known unrelated suggestions in other functions and `internal/billing` would remain unapplied and could be mentioned briefly as separate opportunities. I would not run mutating `go fix ./...` or `go fix ./internal/cache`, because either can rewrite code beyond `Load`. Go 1.27 permits compatible modernizations but does not widen the authorized edit scope.

Proposed commands, run from the target module root (not run in this simulation):

```bash
git status --short
cat go.mod
rg -n 'func .*Load|func Load|Load\(' internal/cache
bash /Users/eugeneshershen/golang-skills/skills/go-code-refactor/scripts/verify-refactor.sh baseline ./...
go fix -diff ./internal/cache
```

After inspecting the actual body, tests, safety-net guidance, and any applicable behavior traps, I would make the small `Load` edit. Existing green tests plus the baseline support this low-risk guard-clause transformation; I would add characterization coverage only if inspection exposes a material uncovered behavior boundary.

```bash
gofmt -w internal/cache/cache.go
git diff -- internal/cache/cache.go
go test ./internal/cache
bash /Users/eugeneshershen/golang-skills/skills/go-code-refactor/scripts/verify-refactor.sh after ./...
bash /Users/eugeneshershen/golang-skills/skills/go-code-refactor/scripts/verify-refactor.sh diff
git diff --check
git diff --stat
```

I would inspect the diff and retain only the intended function change, preserving any pre-existing user changes. Baseline/final verification is module-wide; the mutation scope remains one function. I would report actual verification results and limitations once observed, without presenting a test-result match as an exhaustive proof of equivalence.

## B: Independently configured policies

I would retain these three functions. Their common switch shape is small, and the scenario explicitly says these policies need to change independently. A shared selector, shared numerical constant, or making `GraceDays` call `RetryLimit` would couple coincidentally equal values. The remaining duplication has a concrete reason: separate policy ownership and future change. No shared abstraction removes meaningful common computation here.

Retained snippet, formatted for display:

```go
func UploadLimit(plan string) int {
	switch plan {
	case "pro":
		return 100
	default:
		return 10
	}
}

func RetryLimit(plan string) int {
	switch plan {
	case "pro":
		return 10
	default:
		return 3
	}
}

func GraceDays(plan string) int {
	switch plan {
	case "pro":
		return 10
	default:
		return 3
	}
}
```

No implementation or verification commands are proposed for this snippet-only no-change result. Unknown plans continue to use each function's own default. The repeated literals remain independent policy values.
